title: Super Blood Harvest (Omnibus) - Taking a look at this wonderfully illustrated artistic RPG module
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xwLoo8ThKHI

Daniel (@dungeondive) flips through *Super Blood Harvest*, the omnibus of "artistic RPG modules" from Dirk with a Vengeance (artist of *Silent Titans*), collecting three escalating adventures — *Escape from the Bloodship*, *Crashed on the Moon* and *Killbot Guardian Gods* — into one lavishly illustrated, isometric, vampire-space-imperium sourcebook. He admires the strong old-videogame isometric look and, crucially, finds this far more *runnable* than the overwhelming *Silent Titans*: a rules-light system (three stats, saving throws on a d20-under, damage without to-hit rolls, an injury table that costs you body parts) that keeps the focus on story over crunch. He walks the bloodship's oxygen rooms and blood-filled "hamster tubes," the lunar temple of the second module, and the sprawling Mars sandbox of the third, where escalating threats drive the campaign. Throughout he floats a wish: that these artist-driven books came as *solo gamebooks*, since the referee is otherwise the only person who gets to enjoy the 90% of them that is the art. A cool, sword-and-planet-flavoured curio.

----

Art-first RPG zines like this put nearly all the beauty in the GM's hands. Do they work better shared around a table, or reimagined as solo gamebooks?
